*681. DRALLADIPRAJKUM:† 
SHRIMATIN.P DURGA : 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether in an International symposium on plant pathogens held at ierabad 
in January, 2003, if was claimed that toxity of cow's urine is equivalent hat of several 
known fungicides and pesticides, etc.; 
(b) if so, whether Government have ordered further research in this regard; 
(c) the research institutes which have been assigned this work? 
THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE (SHRIAJIT SINGH): (a) to (c) A ;ment 
is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) In a National Symposium (not International) on "Plant Pathogens crsity in 
Relation to Plant Health" held at Osmania University, Hyderabad ing 16-18 
January, 2003 it has been claimed by the Scientists of the Faculty of riculture, 
Annamalai University that Cow's urine was effective against two

RAJYA S ABHA [9 May, 2003] 
plant pathogens under in vitro conditions. However, no fungicides were 
compared with cow's urine by these workers. 
(b) and (c) Similar work has been done at several places in the country but without 
much success when tested in the field. For example Central Rice Research Institute, Cuttack 
has conducted a replicated field trial to examine the effectiveness of Cow's Urine on bacterial 
leaf blight - an important disease of rice. It was found that the cow's urine has no effect in 
controlling the disease under field conditions. However, field evaluation of effectiveness of 
cow's urine is being continued at a few Institutes of the Indian Council of 
Agricultural Research and State Agricultural Universities viz:—  
1. Central Institute for Subtropical Horticulture, Lucknow; 
2. National Research Centre for Soybean, Indore; and 
3. G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar. 
DR. ALLADI  P. RAJKUMAR: Sir, the main purpose of my raising this 
question is that recently an international symposium was held in Hyderabad on "Plant 
Pathogens". One of the articles published in that regard has given rise to my question. 
One of the scientists from Annamalai University of Tamil Nadu, who has presented a 
paper, claimed that cow's urine has got toxic contents which, can kill fungus. But 
the answer given by the hon. Minister is that the Central Rice Research Institute, 
Cuttack has conducted a field trial to examine the effectiveness of cow's urine on 
bacterial leaf blight - an important disease of rice. It was found that the cow's urine has 
no effect in controlling the disease under field conditions. The scientist who has 
conducted this research and published papers in this regard strongly believed in it. 
So, I request the hon. Minister to provide financial assistance for further research and 
to probe into the issue. 
SHRIAJIT SINGH: Sir, the answer states that it was a national symposium, not an 
international symposium. It also says that no fungicides were compared with cow's 
urine by these workers. The only thing that was mentioned is that two plant 
pathogens under test conditions were found effective. As the hon. Member has said, 
there are three institutes where this research is going on. We know only these three 
institutes; it may be going on in some more universities and other places. 
DRALLADIP. RAJKUMAR: Sir, I have the proofthat it was an international 
symposium. I will give it to the hon. Minister. Let him clarify whether the 
international symposium is wrong or he himself is wrong.

†*683. DR. A.K. PATEL : Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the number of women benefited under the "Swadhar Yojana" formulated for 
women living in difficult conditions; 
(b) the State-wise details thereof; and 
(c) whether it has ever been investigated that the benefit which is received by the 
women is being provided appropriately? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT PR MURU 
MANOHAR JOSHI): (a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
The scheme was operauonalised in 2001-2002, one project was sanctioned in 2001-
2002 and 21 in 2002-2003. Out of these one project was sanctioned to CSWB, eight to 
State Governments and their organisations and 13 to voluntary organisations 
recommended by State Governments. Details are annexed in Statement-I (See below). 
About 3000 women are expected to be benefited directly. 
In addition to usual checks and balances built in every scheme the following 
are additional safeguards to ensure that the benefit accrue to the intended 
beneficiaries: 
(i) The State Government is expected to forward the proposal after it is 
considered in a high level committee in order to ensure the antecedents of the 
implementing organisations, to ensure the necessary linkages with different agencies 
like Police, Welfare, Health are forged and that difFerent components are built in. This 
high level committee would also monitor the implementation. 
(ii) The State Secretary is required to make a presentation before projects of the 
state are considered. 
(iii) Some of the projects in Delhi and Rajasthan are being monitored by Delhi 
High Court.

MANOHAR JOSffl): (a) to (e) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) to (e) Guidelines have been issued by the Cabinet Secretariat in December 1999 
regarding clearance for study/research schemes involving foreigners/foreign collaboration 
from security/sensitivity angle and by the Ministry of Home Affairs in September 2000 
regarding security clearance for holding international conferences/seminars/workshop 
etc. in India. The guidelines which have been issued by Ministry of Human Resource

Universities to enter into an MoU with foreign Universities/Institutes with prior

scholars/students coming to India or their academic activities. The guidelines lay

5133. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:Will the Minister of AGRICULTURAL 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the country has been experiencing poor rains 
during the last five years; 
(b) if so, the man made reasons therefore and the rain prospects this year; 
(c) whether Government have assessed the impact of poor rains on rural 
income and its purchasing power;. 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the steps being taken to ensure sufficient availability of water for 
agricultural production? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI 
HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV): (a) and (b) The monsoon rains in the 
76 

[9 May, 2003] RAJYASABHA 
country have been less than Long Period Average (LPA) in four out of past five years. 
According to the revised classification of monsoon rainfall for the country as a whole, 
the rainfall was below normal (90 to 97% of LPA) inl 999,2000 &2001 and in drought 
category (less than 90% of LPA) in 2002. In 1998, the monsoon 
rainfall was above normal (103 to 110% of LPA). 
There is no evidence of long term trend in South-west monsoon rainfall 
which can be attributed to man-made reasons. The inter annual fluctuations are with in 
the natural variability of monsoon phenomenon. 
Based upon the newly adopted 8-Parameter Power Regression Model, India 
Meteorological Department (IMD's) long range forecast for the 2003 Southwest 
Monsoon Season (June-September) is that the rainfall for the country as a whole is 
likely to be 96% of the LPA with a model error of ±5%. 
(c) and (d) The impact of poor rains on rural income and its purchasing power 
is mainly due to adverse impact on agricultural production. However, the temporal and 
spatial distribution of rainfall is equally important. During 2001, monsoon rainfall 
was 8% less than LPA for the country as a whole, nevertheless, the agricultural 
production was an all time high for foodgrains. During 2002, the monsoon rainfall 
was abnormally low, especially in July, which is the most agriculturally active 
month; this led to sharp decline in agricultural production in respect of most of the 
crops. The resultant adverse impact on farm economy was assessed and accordingly 
drought relief allowance over and above the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for 
important rabi and kharif crops was announced. 
(e) In order to augment the availability of water in country for irrigation and other 
uses and for their efficient use, a large number of dams have been constructed thereby 
creating 177 billion cubic metre (BCM) of storage capacity. Another 75 BCM of 
storage will be created on completion of dams which are under various stages of 
construction. Proposals to take up additional dams to create a live storage capacity of 
132 BCM are also under formulation/consideration. To accelerate creation of 
irrigation of potential by early completion of ongoing schemes, Government has 
launched Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme (AIBP). Central Ground Water 
Board has also taken up a Central Sector Scheme on "Studies of Recharge to Ground 
Water" on pilot basis. Assistance is also being extended to State Government under 
Command Area Development (CAD) Programme for bridging the gap between 
potential created and utilized. For meeting future requirements of water, as a long 
term measure, National Water Development Agency have formulated National 
Perspective Plan for water resources development which envisages interlinking 
various Peninsular rivers 
77 

RAJYA SABHA [9 May, 2003J 
and Himalayan rivers for transfer of water from surplus basins to water deficit basins. 
The Government is conscious of the need to ensure for efficient use of water for 
agriculture, which in essence is an integral part of sustainable development of 
agriculture as enshrined in the National Policy on Agriculture. Efforts aimed at 
diversification of agriculture constitute an important initiative in this direction, because this 
would facilitate the much-needed shift from the rice-wheat system in areas suffering 
from the stress on ground water resources. Further, priority is accorded to the holistic 
and sustainable development of semi-arid rainfed areas through integrated watershed 
development approach in which the construction of micro irrigation facilities like water 
harvesting structures, village ponds, check dams, etc. are promoted.

Liter cy rate 
5185.SHRI SURESH PACHOURI: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that so far literacy rates are concerned there are wide 
inter and intra State differences; 
(b) if so, the details thereof with literacy rates among male and female 
separately; and 
(c) the steps taken by Government to improve the situation so far female 
literacy rates, especially in Northern States are concerned ? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIASHOK PRADHAN): (a) and (b) A statement giving 
State-wise break up of literacy rates of males and females in 1991 and 2001 is 
annexed. (See below). 
(c) The steps taken by Government under various Schemes to improve 
female literacy rates are as follows: 
(1) Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan 
A new Scheme of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) has been launched to 
implement Universalization of Elementary Education. The goals of SSA are as 
follows: 
• All children in school/Education Guarantee Scheme center, Alternate 
school, back to school camp by 2003. 
• All children complete five years primary education by 2007. 
• All children complete eight years of schooling by 2010. 
• Focus on Elementary Education of satisfactory quality with emphasis 
on education for life. 
• Bridge all gender and social gaps at primary stage by 2007 and at 
Elementary Education level by 2010. 
• Universal retention by 2010. 
122 

[9 May, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
In addition, some of the special interventions included for the girl child are: 
• Intervention for early Childhood Care and Education. 
• School/EGS like alternative facility to be set up within one kilometre of all 
habitations. 
• Upgradation of EGS to regular schools. 
• Special mainstreaming camps for out-of-school girls/SC/ST children 
under the alternative and innovative Education Component. 
• Provision of process based community participation with a focus on the 
participation of women and SC/ST. 
• Provision of contact specific innovative intervention for girls' 
education and education of SC/ST children upto Rs. SO lakhs in a district 
in a particular year in which the ceiling for each intervention is Rs. 15 
lakhs. 
• Mid-day meal programme. 
• Incentives like uniforms and scholarships to be funded from State Plan 
only. 
• Adequate Teaching Learning Equipment for all Primary and Upper 
Primary schools. 
• Atleast 50% of the teachers to be appointed have to be women. 
• Special teaching support as per need. 
• Using Community Teachers. 
• Provision of free textbooks to all girl/SC/ST children at primary and upper 
primary level with an upper ceiling of Rs. 150/- per child. 
(2) Mahila Samakhya 
Manila Samakhya Programme has been in operation since 1989. It is a 
women's empowerment project and endeavours to create an environment for women 
to seek knowledge and information in order to make informed choices. The 
principal strategy is to organize women into collectives called Mahila Sanghas to 
identify their needs and evolve collective ways to deal with their problems. 
Currently, the Mahila Samakhya programme is operating in 60 districts 
covering more than 9000 villages in 10 states of Uttar Pradesh, Kamataka, Gujarat, 
Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Bihar, Madh ya Pradesh, Assam, Jharkhand and 
Uttaranchal. 
(3) National Literacy Mission 
Under National Literacy Mission (NLM) focus is given on female literacy. 
Special innovative projects are being taken up to raise the level of female literacy in 
low female literacy areas. Special efforts are being made to target female 
Panchayati Raj functionaries and make them literate.

control of the State Government concerned. The cases of crime on Railways are 
reported to, registered and investigated by the Government Railway Police. 
The Railway Administration coordinates with the GRP so that the security of the 
passengers may be ensured. Though the responsibility to curb these incidents lies 
with the State Governments, the railways also taken the following steps to supplement 
the efforts of the State Governments.

detraining from the coaches.

4. Wherever the State Government wants to establish mobile post in the running 
trains, necessary facilities like accommodation etc. are provided. 
5. FIR forms are mac's available with the Train Guards/Station Masters/ RPF to 
facilitate the travelling public to lodge their reports immediately. 
6. RPF Assistance Posts are provided at important stations to assist 
passengers in lodging FIRs with Government Railway Police.

These are in Gujarat (Mocha village, Porbandar District); Madhya Pradesh (ten 
villages in five districts viz. Jabalpur, Raisen, Guna, Indore and Bhopal); 
Maharashtra (two villages namely Kurur and Varsoli of Raigad District) and

Zones). The fifth bio-village project is being operated at Pondicherry by the 
M.S. Swaminathan Research Foundation, Chennai with support from the United 
Nations Development Programmes.

fertilisers and Bio-pesticides; vermicomposting; cultivation of mushroom, 
spirulina and high yielding sugarcane varieties; aquaculture including 
pisciculture and prawn rearing; and sericulture. Post-harvest technologies, 
development of entrepreneurship in vegetable dyes and herbal products have 
also been included. Many of components which are highly region/location-
specific, are tailored to the needs of the local stakeholders, Beneficiaries/target 
groups have also been identified. There has been a positive response from the 
target population.

basis of merit, suitability to the region and their relevance to the target group.

5258. SHRI PARMESHWAR KUMAR AGARWALLA: Will the Minister of 
YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state : 
(a) whether the National Commission for youth was initially set up for six 
months; 
(b) if so, the reasons which prompted Government to grant extension; 
(c) the composition of the Commission and its functions; 
(d) whether the Commission has submitted any interim report; and 
(e) if not, the reasons therefor ? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI VIKRAM 
VERMA):(a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) The reasons for extending the tenure of the Commission for one more 
year were as under :—  
(i) The Commission was set up vide Resolution dated 15.3.02. However, it 
could start functioning only w.e.f. July 2002 on account of logistics 
constraints, such as, accommodation and appointment of a nucleus of 
staff. 
(ii) A full-time Member-Secretary joined the Commission on the 27th June, 
2002 only. 
(iii) Except for one, who was Delhi- based, all members (four) had been 
working from outside Delhi, initially. 
(iv) The work of the Commission involves collection and compilation of 
voluminous information/data, consultation and study, meetings with 
various Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, State 
Governments, Youth Organisations and NGOs. More time was needed 
to complete the above tasks. 
(c) A copy each of the composition and terms of reference of the 
Commission is attached as Statement-I and Statement-II respectively (See below).

of any interim report.

Performance of hockey and football players 
5261. SHRI SHANKAR ROY CHOWDHURY: Will the Minister of YOUTH 
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether any formalised structure exists to assess the performance of young 
football and hockey players during the National trophy events like the Subroto Cup 
and Junior Nehru Cup; 
(b) the arrangements for proper follow-up and training programmes 
thereafter for the players; and 
(c) whether there are plans to extend astro-turf facilities for coaching and training 
of junior hockey players at Kolkata, other than theexisting one at Salt Lake Stadium ? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI VJKRAM 
VERMA) : (a) and (b) Yes Sir, Subroto Mukherjee Sports Education Society 
(SMSES) has set up a formalised structure which not only conducts the tournament 
but also ensures follow-up of selected players with regard to their recruitment in IAF, 
award of Government scholarship by Netaji Subhash Institute of Sports (NSNIS), 
Patiala/Sports Authority of India (SAT) and spotting of talents by other agencies. The 
Society constitutes a three member Selection Committee to assess the young 
footballers comprising of representative of All India Football Federation, a 
representative of Sports Authority of India, and a representative of Subroto Mukherjee 
Sports Education Society. The Selection Committee selects outstanding players from 
junior and sub-junior players and forwards their names to NIS, Patiala. The Society 
also awards scholarship @ Rs.2500/- per annum to selected players. 
As regards Hockey, it is stated that there is no such tournament known as Junior 
Nehru Cup. However, Jawaharlal Nehru Hockey Tournament Society (JNHTS) 
organises 5 tournaments every year in Delhi viz; Sub-junior (Boys under-15), Junior 
(Boys under-17), Girls (under-17), Championship Colleges Hockey Tournament and 
Main Open Tournament for meii: JNHTS also has a formalised structure to assess the 
performance of players during the junior hockey tournaments. For this purpose, 
there is a Committee headed by an Olympian, representative from Sports Authority of 
India (SAI), representative from Indian Hockey Federation (IHF) and two nominees 
from JNHTS. 
Arrangements for proper follow-up and training of the sportspersons are done by 
the respective societies. The talent identified from these tournaments are eligible for 
national level scholarships under the Scholarship Scheme of the Government of India. 
Scholarship is given subject to the condition that identified talent is not under any 
approved training scheme of SAI or State Government. As such, the identified talent is 
also taken by SAI for training under its various schemes. 
(c) No, Sir.

Foreign Direct Investment in Electronic Media 
SHRI   MANOJ   BHATTACHARYA  (West  Bengal):   Sir,   I  call  the 
attention of the hon. Minister of Information and Broadcasting to the issue 
225 

RAJYA SABHA [9 May, 2003] 
of foreign direct investment in electronic media in particular.   Thank you. 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF INFORMATION 
AND BROADCASTING (SHRI RAVI SHANKAR PRASAD): Sir. I will present 
before the hon. House a brief statement about the entire gamut. The hon. 
Members have drawn my attention to their concerns over the entry of foreign 
companies in the electronic media in our country. Let me inform this hon. 
House about the decision taken by the Government. 
I would like to make a brief statement on the existing regime as well 
as the present status in respect of various service segments. 
1. Cable Network Service 
As per the provisions of the Cable Television Network (Regulation) 
Act, 1995, no licence is required but a 'person' is required to be registered as a 
cable operator with the Head Postmaster of a Head Post Office of the area 
concerned. A person means, - (i) a n individual who is a citizen of India; (ii) an 
association of individuals or body of individuals, whether incorporated or not, 
whose members are citizens of India; and (iii) a company in which not less 
than 51 per cent of the paid-up share capital is held by the citizens of India. 
2. Direct-to-Home Broadcasting Service (DTH) 
The Government took a decision to start the DTH in the country in 
November 2000 after the Group of Ministers had deliberated and considered 
all the issues connected thereto at length. Detailed guidelines for starting DTH 
service were issued by the Government on 15th March, 2001. 
So far, only three applications for starting DTH broadcasting service 
have been received.  They are from, 
i) Space T.V. Private Limited 
ii) A.S.C. Enterprises Limited, and 
iii) Essel Shyam Communication Limited. 
226 

[9 May, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
The eligibility criteria under the DTH are: 
(a) Applicant-company to be an Indian company registered 
under the Companies Act, 1956. 
(b) Total foreign equity holding (including FDI/NRI/OCB/FII) in 
the uplinking company not to exceed 49 per cent. 
(c) Within the foreign equity, the FDI component not to exceed 
20 per cent. The quantum represented by the proportion of 
the paid-up equity share capital to the total issued equity 
capital of the Indian promoter company, held or controlled 
by the foreign investors through FDI/NRI/OCB investments 
shall form part of the abovesaid FDI limit of 20 per cent. 
All these applications are under process. 
3. Uplinking Policy 
I am reading out a gist of the policy module for uplinking.   These are: 
(a) For setting up of uplinking hub/teleports, the company has

RAJYA SABHA [9 May, 2003] 
STATEMENT BY MINISTER 
Successful launch of second test flight of Geo-synchronous Satellite Launch 
Vehicle, GSLV - D2 from Sriharikota 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING, THE 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF STATISTICS AND 
PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION AND THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
DEPARTMENT OF ATOMIC ENERGY AND DEPARTMENT OF SPACE (SHRI 
SATYABRAT MOOKHERJEE): Madam, I am happy to inform this august 
House that the second test flight of GSLV-D2 was successfully carried out 
from Satish Dhawan Space Centre, SHAR, Sriharikota on May 08, 2003. 
GSLV-D2 is a three-stage vehicle. It uses solid propellant first stage 
with four liquid strap-ons and a liquid propellant second stage. While the 
cryogenic third stage has been supplied by Russia, the control guidance and 
electronics for the stage have been designed, developed and implemented by 
ISRO scientists. The 49 metre tall technologically complex GSLV-D2, weighing 
400 tonnes, lifted off at 4.58 pm carrying GSAT-2 Satellite. After a perfect 
count down and about 17 minutes of smooth flight, GSAT-2 spacecraft was 
successfully placed into its intended orbit. GSLV-D2 has significantly 
demonstrated a payload capability of 1825 kg., which is about 300 kg. more 
than what was launched in the first flight. This was made possible by 
improvements such as the use of higher pressure engines for strap-ons, 
introduction of improved propellant loading for the core solid stage and 
optimisation of structural elements. This successful GSLV-D2 flight has 
validated the various technologies demonstrated during the first flight as well 
as improvements made for the second flight. 
The first signals acquired from the GSAT-2 satellite indicate normal 
health of the satellite. GSAT-2 will be raised to its final geo-synchronous orbit 
in the coming days followed by deployment of its solar arrays and antennae. 
The satellite, in addition to carrying transponders for communication and 
mobile satellite services, has four scientific experiments. 
With this successful flight of GSLV-D2, the payload capability has 
been established for launching operational communication satellites of 2000 
kg. class. Accomplishment of this technologically-challenging mission is the 
culmination of efforts of ISRO Centres supported by industries and academic 
institutions in India.

Sir, this was a momentous Session and, as a responsible Opposition 
party, we have co-operated in the passage of the important financial 
legislation. But that does not mean that we do not have worries about the 
current state of our economy, or, the way it is being managed. We have grave 
worries about the fiscal situation in our country and also the overall economic
